verdicts.quote: “DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token…”
verdicts.reason: Vendor docs explicitly describe OAuth2 client credentials for obtaining the bearer used on all API requests; the UI‑provisioned “API key” is part of that OAuth flow, not a standalone auth scheme. ([api.docs.dealcloud.com](https://api.docs.dealcloud.com/docs/token?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Get in touch with your account manager to have Publications enabled on your site.”
verdicts.reason: Access is provisioned inside an existing customer tenant (per‑site Swagger, admin‑gated API keys) and certain API features require AM/CSM enablement—there’s no public self‑serve developer signup. ([api.docs.dealcloud.com](https://api.docs.dealcloud.com/docs/publications/getting_started?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Our APIs are organized into functional areas… Authentication… User Management… Schema… Data… Backups… Publications… Relationship Intelligence.”
verdicts.reason: Docs show many functional areas and CRUD over core objects (e.g., “The Rows APIs allow you to create, retrieve, update, and delete records”), indicating a broad surface. ([api.docs.dealcloud.com](https://api.docs.dealcloud.com/docs))

verdicts.quote: “# DealCloud MCP Server … A compatible AI assistant connects to the DealCloud MCP Server and signs in as the user.”
verdicts.reason: DealCloud publishes and documents its own MCP server on the official docs site, indicating an official vendor MCP. ([api.docs.dealcloud.com](https://api.docs.dealcloud.com/mcp))

verdicts.quote: “Local clients must be enabled for your site before they can connect. Contact your DealCloud Account Manager to have ‘localhost’ redirects enabled.”
verdicts.reason: An agent toolkit is buildable now, but practical use depends on being a customer and on admin/AM enablement (plus short‑lived tokens), so there are operational caveats rather than hard blockers. ([api.docs.dealcloud.com](https://api.docs.dealcloud.com/mcp/connections))
